entities.summary: Viswanathan Shanta was an Indian oncologist and the chairperson of the Adyar Cancer Institute, Chennai. She is best known for her efforts towards making quality and affordable cancer treatment accessible to all patients in her country. She dedicated herself to the mission of organizing care for cancer patients, study of the disease, research on its prevention and cure, spreading awareness about the disease, and developing specialists and scientists in various subspecialties of oncology. Her work won her several awards, including the Magsaysay Award, Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Vibhushan, the second highest civilian award given by the Government of India.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Viswanathan Shanta's work on making quality and affordable cancer treatment accessible to all patients in India has had a significant regional impact, particularly for marginalized communities. Her efforts have saved countless lives and improved the overall cancer care landscape in South Asia.
